policy: Hand-labelled gold for index-time mention extraction, adjudicated against the Spanish text block of each speech. A speech's expected_deputies are the catalog deputies NAMED in that text, by canonical 'Apellido, Nombre'. Labelling rules: (1) include a deputy when a knowledgeable reader identifies a UNIQUE catalog referent from the text/context — full names ('Pedro Sánchez', 'María Jesús Montero') and unambiguous role/prose references ('el señor Bravo' = the PP spokesman Juan Bravo). Parenthesized stenographer annotations — '(Aplausos.—El señor <Apellido>: …)' — are NOT part of the mention surface: extraction strips them before NER and mines them into Speech.interruptions instead, so a person named ONLY inside annotations is expected as an interruption, never as a mention (re-adjudicated 2026-07-14; before the annotation-stripping change such names counted as mentions); (2) EXCLUDE surnames genuinely ambiguous between several catalog holders where context cannot disambiguate (e.g. the two 'Lago Peñas'); (3) EXCLUDE homonyms whose referent is NOT the catalog deputy — ex-PMs (Aznar, Zapatero, Casado), regional presidents (Illa, Mazón, Moreno Bonilla, 'presidente Clavijo' = Canarias), historical/other figures ('Franco', judge 'Macías', aide 'Paco Salazar'), foreign leaders (Milei), and first names in lists ('Joan'); (4) the speaker's own name counts only if it actually appears in the spoken text (rare — e.g. quoting an opponent's attacks on them). Empty lists are intentional precision cases. NON-DEPUTY labels: `expected_non_deputies` lists people named who are not sitting deputies but ARE covered by the person catalog — government ministers, the King, autonomous-community presidents, former prime ministers, foreign leaders, and curated notable figures (e.g. Aldama, Begoña Gómez). Names use the catalog's canonical form. Scope is the catalog: figures it does not cover stay unlabelled and are deliberate true-negatives, not recall misses — the dictator Franco, the judiciary (magistrates, the fiscal general), and people not (yet) curated (e.g. Casado, Calviño). A missing `expected_non_deputies` defaults to an empty list. This gold is INDEPENDENT of the system: it records mentions a reader confirms, so deputies the current NER/resolver misses (uncommon surnames, given-name+surname partials like 'Cuca Gamarra', ambiguity-guard drops like 'el señor Bravo') are kept as true positives to measure recall honestly. Sample: 73 speeches. M1-M43 are stratified over initiative types 162/172/173/210 and co-official-language originals (ca/gl/eu, whose Spanish translation block is scanned). M44-M73 extend the set so that honorific-only address is measurable at all: the original 43 do contain ambiguous-surname drops, but in every one the person is also named in a longer form in the same speech, so any context-based disambiguation scores exactly zero there. The extension was selected SYSTEM-INDEPENDENTLY — by a regex for a gendered honorific plus a surname borne by two or more catalog people, regardless of whether the resolver gets it right — in three strata: 18 positives where a deputy is addressed only as 'la señora X' throughout (M56-M73), 8 precision controls carrying a bare given name the ambiguity guard drops and must keep dropping (M48-M55), and 4 shared-surname speeches (M44-M47). For an honorific-only address, the 'unique catalog referent' of rule 1 is settled by the sitting: 'la señora Muñoz' is the member who put the question minutes earlier, which a parliamentary reader knows and the resolver does not. M56 and M57 additionally name a minister whose office changed mid-term (Aagesen), and M17/M38 were relabelled for that class — it was invisible to this metric until duplicate bootstrap entries stopped making such ministers unmentionable.
